subject: Aligning Dedicated GPUs with Q2 usage — renewal coming up
messages:
From: Sophie Lane <sophie.lane@orbishealth.com>
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.com
Cc: Jacob Rhee <jacob.rhee@orbishealth.com>, contracts@orbishealth.com
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 09:21:00 -0700
Subject: Aligning Dedicated GPUs with Q2 usage — renewal coming up

Diego —

Hope you’re well. Our renewal window for the dedicated fleet is in three weeks and the team asked me to check usage before we lock the next commit. We attached our usage export for Q1 (hourly GPU utilization and job mix). High-level notes from our infra team: average utilization of committed pool is ~63%, peak windows hit 92% for short bursts, and cost is trending up due to retry-heavy pipelines.

We’re open to either increasing the dedicated commit if it buys us lower unit cost, or moving some workloads to a burst pool to avoid a large long-term commit. Can your team propose 1) a small-step amendment to cover predicted peaks, and 2) a conservative plan if we expect a 20% growth next quarter?

Attaching: orbis_usage_report_Q1.csv

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call if that helps.

—Sophie
Sophie Lane
Head of ML Infrastructure, Orbis Health
Sophie.lane@orbishealth.com
From: diego_fernandez@redwood.com
To: Sophie Lane <sophie.lane@orbishealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 12:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Aligning Dedicated GPUs with Q2 usage — renewal coming up

Sophie —

Thanks for the export, that’s exactly what we need. I’ve looped in Marissa (your account exec) and Ben (strategic sales) plus Laura from our provisioning team so we can put together a short options matrix.

Quick asks from our side to speed analysis: could you confirm which workloads must remain on Dedicated (PHI-sensitive model serving) vs which can tolerate burst? Also, any expected model size changes (e.g., moving to 70B models) in the next 90 days?

Proposed next steps:
- Marissa & Laura will run a two-scenario sizing (conservative growth + peak-protection) and produce a 2-option quote (incremental commit vs commit + burst buffer).
- I’ll assemble a one-page mutual action plan with dates for amendment, provisioning window, and billing proration.
- If that looks good, Ben will send the amendment draft and DocuSign link.

Can we target a review by Thursday (4/15)? I can block 30 minutes that afternoon.

Thanks,
Diego
Director, Strategic GTM Operations
Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: Sophie Lane <sophie.lane@orbishealth.com>, diego_fernandez@redwood.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 10:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Aligning Dedicated GPUs with Q2 usage — renewal coming up

Sophie —

Thanks for the data. I ran a quick pass with Laura and attached a short proposal (provisioning_proposal_v2.pdf) with two concrete options:

Option A — Moderate commit increase
- Add 12 A100-equivalent GPUs to the Dedicated pool (effective immediately on amendment).
- Expected impact: raises steady-state availability, reduces queuing during peaks, estimated utilization post-change ~72%.
- Term: 12 months; unit price = $X / GPU / month; annualized delta = ~$YYk.

Option B — Hybrid burst buffer + smaller commit
- Add 6 Dedicated GPUs + a configurable 8-GPU burst pool that can be consumed at a premium rate during peaks.
- Expected impact: keeps committed spend lower, covers short peaks, estimated steady utilization ~66% with safe headroom.
- Term: 12 months; burst pricing applies only when consumed; projected blended cost lower than Option A unless peak hours exceed current observed burst windows.

Notes and mitigations
- We can enable prefix/KV caching on your serving tier to reduce tokenized compute for long-tail requests — Laura can share configuration steps (no infra downtime).
- If you expect model-size increases, Option A is better for latency-sensitive serving; Option B is best if you want fiscal flexibility.

Attached: provisioning_proposal_v2.pdf (pricing table + rollout milestones)

If you’re available Thur 4/15 at 3:00pm PT I can walk through the options with the team.

—Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: Sophie Lane <sophie.lane@orbishealth.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.com, diego_fernandez@redwood.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 08:54:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Aligning Dedicated GPUs with Q2 usage — renewal coming up

Sophie —

Appreciate the quick review yesterday. Per our call, I’m attaching an amendment draft (amendment_draft-RDW-3421.docx) and a one-page mutual action plan below. The amendment includes proration for the mid-cycle add and the Burst pool clause for limited-duration consumption.

Mutual action plan (high level)
- 2027-04-15: Review & sign amendment (DocuSign link: https://docusign.redwood.com/RDW-3421)
- 2027-04-20: Provision Dedicated GPUs (12) or Commit+Burst as per chosen option
- 2027-04-30: Operationalize caching & batch settings; engineering checklist owned by Laura
- 2027-06-15: Usage check-in and optional re-profile for Q3 commit sizing

If you want, we can put a soft cap on monthly spend for the Burst pool (alerting + auto-throttle) — that’s something we can add to the amendment.

I’ll await confirmation of Option A vs B and will issue the DocuSign package once you confirm.

Best,
Ben Carter
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Sophie Lane <sophie.lane@orbishealth.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, diego_fernandez@redwood.com
Cc: Jacob Rhee <jacob.rhee@orbishealth.com>, contracts@orbishealth.com
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Aligning Dedicated GPUs with Q2 usage — renewal coming up

Team —

Thanks — we’ll take Option B (6 dedicated + 8 burst) to preserve budget flexibility while smoothing peaks. Two asks before we sign: please add the burst soft cap (monthly cap + alerting) to the amendment, and prorate the effective date to 4/20 so we only pay for the days provisioned in April.

Jacob from procurement is looped on cc and will manage the signature & PO; contracts@orbishealth.com will review the amendment. I’ll sign the DocuSign once the burst cap language is included — please send the revised DocuSign link when ready.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

—Sophie
